name: What is the difference between a full kitchen and a kitchenette in an ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a full kitchen and a kitchenette in an ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full kitchen in an ADU includes a complete range of amenities: a full-sized sink, refrigerator, stove/oven, and often a dishwasher, along with ample counter space and storage. It is designed for comprehensive meal preparation and daily living. A kitchenette, conversely, is a smaller, more compact cooking area, typically featuring a smaller sink, a mini-refrigerator, and possibly a microwave or a two-burner cooktop. It's suitable for light meal prep and is often found in studio ADUs or guest suites where space is limited. Local regulations may define minimum requirements for each.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full kitchen has a complete range of appliances for full meal prep, while a kitchenette is smaller with fewer appliances, suitable for light cooking. Local regulations often define minimum requirements for each type.
